A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PEARL and CalConflictBench work. Their main text, equations, seven figures, three tables, and Appendices A–E are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CalConflictBench evaluations, PEARL training results, parameter analyses, and a model-response case study in Tables 1–2, Figures 2–5, and Appendix D.3.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark evaluations, PEARL results, parameter analyses, and appendix case study.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 5 retain the same StrategyHub rollout, four reward components, curriculum, and round-wise GRPO training. The expanded abstract explains existing components; the reward-symbol corrections do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic calendar-conflict coverage: ten evaluation users from two organizations and training-data construction using four organizations with ten users each. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same base models, ReAct, and Mem+ReAct. Table 2 retains zero-shot, SFT, and zero-shot plus StrategyHub comparisons. The newly cited planning methods are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the reported ORD rank-index range from {0,...,M} to {0,...,M−1}. This is a limited metric-specification correction: the formula, evaluation procedures, splits, context settings, and training budgets remain unchanged, with no rerun established.

E4.justification: The conflict-count and context-window analyses in Figure 2, adaptation curves, and Appendix D.3 doctor-appointment versus SEV2 case study are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or error analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains averaging over ten independent instances, and Figure 5 retains the same shaded bands. Neither version changes seed/run reporting, uncertainty definitions, or significance-testing practices.

E6.justification: All result-table entries, plotted results, and case-study outcomes are unchanged. Table 2 reports PEARL AER 0.12 and ERR 0.761 in both versions, versus SFT's 0.27 and 0.325.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the formal zero-based rank domain from {0,...,M} to {0,...,M−1}, making it consistent with M candidate events and the stated ORD range [0,1]. Other mathematical definitions and derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same task, benchmark, and PEARL contributions, baseline-adaptation claims, and claimed 55% error-rate improvement. The revised abstract describes existing memory and reward components more explicitly without changing the claims' scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of context limitations, memory-only performance, and reinforcement learning's role are retained. The limitations concerning synthetic preferences, unobserved personal factors, incomplete parameter sweeps, and restricted history remain substantively unchanged, as does Appendix D.3's error interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendices C–E retain the same generation and annotation procedures, prompts, StrategyHub schema, implementation frameworks, hyperparameters, and hardware/runtime disclosures. Table 3 and the project-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds a focused discussion of planning/search and process-reward training, with five new references including Tree of Thoughts and Thought of Search. It explicitly describes test-time preference alignment while retaining the existing calendar-management and memory positioning.

P1.justification: v3 revises parts of the abstract, corrects grammar across the main text, harmonizes StrategyHub reward symbols, expands related-work prose, and adds an acknowledgment. These are localized refinements; the main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: All seven figures and three tables are retained without redesign. Figure 2's caption is edited, Figure 6 shifts columns, and Table 3 moves from a page shared with training text to a standalone final page, alongside other limited reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 improves clarity through abstract and grammar edits, corrects the ORD index bound and inconsistent reward symbols, and provides broader planning/search context. These yield a modest gain in readability and internal consistency; the experimental evidence and substantive applicability limitations remain unchanged.
